text: An asymptomatic 55-year-old undergoing ultrasound for unrelated reasons is found to have gall bladder wall thickening with intramural diverticula (Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses), no gallstones. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: Reassurance and observation, no treatment needed

text: Which imaging finding is most specific for confirming a diagnosis of adenomyomatosis over simple cholelithiasis?
A patient with segmental adenomyomatosis and coexisting symptomatic gallstones is being counselled about disease relationship. What should they be told?

choices.text: The two conditions frequently coexist but no proven causal relationship exists between them
The two conditions are never seen together
